source:
Game Name (working title)
LAST ROUTE
"No one knows why the road is still open."
Core Idea
You and up to 5 friends are driving one truck across a frozen mountain to deliver the last generator core to a dying town.
Without it...
Thousands of people freeze.
So turning back isn't an option.
Core Gameplay Loop
Drive ⬇ Reach checkpoint ⬇ Random event ⬇ Solve it together ⬇ Repair truck ⬇ Continue ⬇ Repeat ⬇ Final escape
The truck almost never stops for long. The journey is the game.
The BIG Hook
The Storm Changes Every Run.
Not just weather.
The storm changes the world.
Examples:
🌨 Heavy snow.
Visibility 5 metres.
🧊 Frozen lake.
Road disappears.
Drive over ice.
Risk breaking through.
🌲 Fallen trees.
Need axes.
⛰ Avalanche.
New road opens.
Old road closes.
📡 Strange radio signal.
Follow it...
Or ignore it.
🏚 Abandoned village appears.
Sometimes.
Not every run.
Every run feels different.
Player Jobs
Everyone naturally gets a role.
🚛 Driver
Can only focus on driving.
🗺 Navigator
Uses map.
Finds routes.
Reads signs.
🔧 Mechanic
Repairs truck.
Keeps engine alive.
Changes tyres.
📦 Scavenger
Searches buildings.
Gets fuel.
Food.
Medicine.
Parts.
🔦 Lookout
Uses binoculars.
Warns about danger.
Nobody is standing around.
The Horror
No zombie waves.
No screaming monster.
Something...
Is following the truck.
It never attacks directly.
Instead...
Fuel disappears.
Doors open.
Lights go out.
Tyre tracks appear beside yours.
Someone knocks...
But nobody is there.
The mystery is the horror.
Mid Game Twist
You discover...
Every abandoned truck looks exactly like yours.
Same number.
Same cargo.
Same scratches.
How?
Nobody knows.
Now players start theorising.
Final Act
The storm gets insane.
Truck barely works.
Visibility almost zero.
Radio cuts in.
Someone says...
"Don't let it overtake you."
Now everyone panics.
You don't even know what "it" is.
Ending
Reach the town.
Unload generator.
Lights come on.
Storm instantly stops.
Outside...
Your truck has six sets of footprints around it.
Nobody says anything.
Game ends.
Players immediately start discussing what happened.
Why I think this is stronger
The mystery is what people remember.
Not:
"Big monster killed me."
But:
"WHY WAS THERE ANOTHER TRUCK?"
Those kinds of mysteries create YouTube theory videos.
MVP (cheap version)
One truck.
One mountain road.
Three checkpoints.
10-15 random events.
One ending.
No giant open world.
No massive AI.
The game could be finished in about 20-30 minutes per run.
But here's the one thing I'd still change.
I wouldn't make it a pure horror game.
I'd make it 70% adventure, 30% horror.
If players are scared the whole time, the fear wears off. If most of the game is about teamwork, driving, and making decisions, then the strange moments hit much harder because they're unexpected.
One last thing: if your goal is a viral Roblox game, don't try to beat Dead Rails by adding more monsters or more mechanics. Beat it by making players ask one question after every run:
"Wait... what actually happened out there?"
That kind of mystery gives people a reason to replay, tell their friends, and watch theory videos. That's much harder to copy than just another survival game.

answers.ask: A mountain road with three checkpoints is a long strip - should it be one region-scale map, or three chapter maps joined at the checkpoints?
answers.answer: Use one compact region-scale mountain road with all three checkpoints along it. The MVP is one road and the journey should feel continuous, not split into separate chapter maps.

answers.ask: Should the abandoned village be a fixed location on the route, or does it need to be omittable since it only appears on some runs?
answers.answer: Make it omittable: it appears only on some runs as a random route-side event/location. It should not be a fixed required stop.

scene_prompt: Create a 3D cooperative adventure map set on one compact, continuous frozen mountain road crossing a stormy alpine region. A single truck route winds through snowbound slopes and tight mountain passes, with three checkpoints spaced along the journey toward a distant dying town in the background, the delivery destination. Route conditions can include deep snow with very short sightlines, a frozen lake crossing where the road vanishes beneath ice, fallen-tree blockages, and avalanche-altered sections where one path is closed and another is exposed. Place scattered abandoned trucks along the route, each visually identical to the players’ truck, plus occasional strange tyre tracks beside the road. An abandoned village sits off the roadside as an omittable, intermittent location rather than a fixed stop, with small buildings that can be searched. Near the final stretch, the road becomes almost obscured by the intensified storm before descending into the town.
blob:
### Genre
Dominant genre: Adventure, with Survival as a secondary horror-pressure register. The continuous delivery journey, checkpoints, and distant destination make Adventure own the route and map shape; the storm and unexplained pursuer contribute atmosphere rather than a separate survival map.

### Shape and preset
Use `route-guided`, following the Guided Trail preset: one continuous mountain-road journey toward a visible destination. Retain the trail and focal-destination logic, but omit its reveal-exit device because the prompt does not describe an outside-to-inside reveal.

### Config requirements
Use `path-trail` as a snow-covered vehicle road winding through passes, exposed slopes, and the lake crossing. Use `landmark-focal` for the distant dying town, visible as a small final destination beyond the storm. Use `terrain-relief` for steep alpine slopes, cliffs, passes, and the final descent. Use `water-body` for the frozen lake where the road disappears under ice. Use `building-interior` for the searchable small buildings in the optional abandoned village.

### Layout requirements
Use `checkpoint-respawn`: place exactly three recovery checkpoints in safe widened roadside pull-offs, spaced at the major thirds of the continuous journey—after the opening pass, beyond the lake/blockage region, and before the final stormbound descent. No hostile emitter is required; the following presence is environmental and unseen.

### Layout components
Build one compact region-scale alpine strip, not separate chapter maps. The route begins at a snowy mountain approach, winds through tight cliffside passes and deep-snow sections, crosses a broad frozen lake, passes fallen-tree and avalanche-altered road segments with one visibly closed branch and one exposed continuation, then enters an almost whiteout-obscured final descent to the town. Scatter identical abandoned trucks at unsettling roadside pull-offs and add intermittent tyre-track traces beside the road. Set the abandoned village in an optional side pocket off the road, with a small cluster of searchable buildings; it is not a required stop or fixed route gate. The boundary is impassable mountain relief, ravines, and storm-blurred outer slopes. Compose the road as a legible S-curve through the frame, with the town held distant near the far end.

### Render order
Use `topdown` first and treat it as authoritative, because every altered road condition must still preserve one driveable continuous route; authored planning is not available outside mazes and racing circuits.

### Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale band: large, driven by a full 20–30 minute vehicle journey across three checkpoints, compressed into one region. Theme: bleak cinematic alpine mystery-horror, blue-grey snowstorm, isolated industrial truck and dying-town lights. Pipeline modifiers: `tiered` for non-overhanging mountain elevation; `P3` because players enter village buildings from the exterior route; `CHECK` for the frozen-lake water feature beneath the traversable ice.
